videos.script: Ask a chat assistant the same question twice, and the two answers may differ. {{twice}} Nothing broke. Each word was drawn from a list of scores, and draws vary. {{draw}} Temperature is the number that shapes that list before the draw. {{shape}} Below one, the likely words get likelier, and the answers settle down. Above one, the scores even out, and rare words start to appear. {{bars}} At zero there is no draw at all. The top word wins, every time. {{zero}} In this lesson you watch toylm's scores sharpen and flatten at three temperatures. {{toylm}} You run the same prompt twice at zero, and get the same sentence. {{same}} Then you sample at a low and a high setting, and see variety arrive with nonsense. {{samples}} By the end you can pick a temperature for a task, and say what it cannot fix. {{choose}}
